Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
928 AM EDT Mon Sep 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A Gale Watch has been issued for the waters around southern
Maryland for the Wednesday into Thursday timeframe.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Cloudy and cooler conditions are expected through mid-week,
  along with daily chances for showers.

- 2) Daily shower chances, abundant cloud cover, and cool 
  temperatures continue through Thursday. Drier this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Cloudy and cooler conditions are expected through
mid-week, along with daily chances for showers.

Conditions will turn out mostly cloudy today. Temperatures will
be cooler than previous days, and conditions will also be less 
humid, with dewpoints dropping into the 60s. There could be a 
substantial gradient in temperatures from northwest to southeast
today. Western Maryland and the West Virginia Panhandle will 
likely struggle to climb out of the 60s with thick cloud cover 
and higher coverage of showers. Locations along and east of I-95
may make it into the upper 70s to near 80 with lower coverage 
of showers and a few more breaks in the cloud cover.

High pressure already in place to our north across southern
Quebec will rapidly strengthen from the upper 1020s hPa today 
to near 1040 hPa by tomorrow night. As this occurs, 
northeasterly flow will strengthen and the CAD wedge in place 
to the east of the Appalachians will strengthen. Large scale 
forcing for ascent will also gradually increase from west to 
east tonight into tomorrow as a shortwave trough and embedded 
upper low approach from the Ohio Valley. As large scale forcing 
for ascent increases, the relatively low coverage of showers 
today will increase substantially heading into tonight, and 
persist through tomorrow, tomorrow night, and Wednesday morning.
At times, the precipitation may even resemble more of a 
continuous stratiform rain shield as opposed to showers.

The flow pattern across the CONUS over the next couple days will
be extremely complex, with a split flow pattern and a closed 
upper-level ridge building to the north of the upper low over 
the Ohio Valley. So while the big picture of the forecast 
tonight through Wednesday has high confidence (low clouds, cool,
and rainy), there is still some forecast uncertainty regarding 
the finer scale details. A few model solutions attempt to 
produce several inches of rainfall over localized areas as we 
become positioned in the right entrance region of a strong jet 
streak developing off to our north and east, but there is lots 
of model to model inconsistency as to if that will occur and 
where. As of now, the most likely scenario appears to be for 
most of the region to receive 1-2 inches of rainfall spread out 
over a prolonged period time tonight through Wednesday morning.
If this were to occur, the rainfall would be beneficial in 
nature given the ongoing drought conditions. However, if the 
solutions that produce isolated totals of 3-6 inches were to 
play out, there could be localized issues with flooding. Even if
the solution with higher end totals plays out, instantaneous 
rainfall rates won't be overly high given the lack of 
instability, so it would be more of a prolonged soaking rainfall
leading to areal flooding, as opposed to thunderstorms 
producing flash flooding. We'll continue to monitor this 
potential as we move forward.

Either way, Tuesday and Wednesday will feature low clouds, 
gusty northeasterly winds, and well below normal temperatures. 
Temperatures likely hold in the 60s on Tuesday, and may even 
struggle to get out of the 50s on Wednesday as the CAD wedge 
reaches its peak strength.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Daily shower chances, abundant cloud cover, and cool
temperatures continue through Thursday. Drier this weekend.

A persistent wedge-like pattern will remain through at least 
Thursday as wedging/blocking high pressure remains up across eastern 
Canada and coastal low pressure strengthens off the Mid-Atlantic 
coast. This will lead to persistent onshore flow as a series of 
shortwave disturbances pivot around the coastal low offshore and the 
remnant stalled frontal boundary south/east of the region. The 
persistent northeast/east fetch off the Atlantic will yield 
continued cloudiness, minor to (potentially moderate) coastal 
flooding (along the western shore of the Chesapeake Bay), cool 
temperatures, and widespread shower chances. 

With a persistent wedge in place, expect highs to struggle to 
get out of the upper 50s and mid 60s through at least Friday. 
Overnight lows will fall into the 40s and 50s given the cool 
maritime airmass overhead.

Coastal low pressure will track northward toward the NJ/Long Island 
coast Friday into Saturday putting more subsidence over the region. 
This will allow for decreasing precipitation chances and rising 
temperatures with highs in the upper 60s and mid 70s. Even with that 
said, model discrepancies remain beyond Saturday as the coastal low 
looks to retrograde in the vicinity of the Mid-Atlantic coast. 
Current 00z members have the low meandering up toward the Jersey 
Shore Saturday before dropping it back south toward the 
Delmarva Sunday into the early part of next week. This would 
lead to abundant cloud cover in place along with continued 
chances for showers, especially in locations east of the Blue 
Ridge/closest to the low pressure system. It's not until the 
middle of next week (i.e September 30th) when the pattern looks 
to flip again as a stronger front looks to cross the region. 
Temperatures will remain near normal through the remainder of 
the extended period with above normal precipitation expected.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
It's a challenging ceiling forecast today with patches of
clearing interspersed with low-end MVFR to high-end IFR. There 
are conflicting signals regarding whether ceilings will lift 
back up to VFR near peak heating today, or how much clouds
continue to fill in. Locations further north and east should 
have the greatest chance of remaining VFR for a few hours this 
afternoon. For now, that is in the TAF at BWI and MTN, but it 
can't be ruled out at DCA or IAD as well. For now, have 
maintained continued MVFR conditions at those sites. AMDs will
likely be needed. Showers may be possible on and off through 
the day. The greater the coverage of those showers, the lesser 
the likelihood that conditions return back to VFR. Winds today 
will generally be out of the north to northeast at around 5-10 
knots.

Guidance is in better agreement that ceilings will lower to IFR
tonight as showers increase in coverage across the area. IFR 
ceilings and on and off showers then continue through the day 
Wednesday. Winds will be out of the northeast tonight through 
Wednesday, and should gust to around 15-25 knots on Tuesday and 
Wednesday.

Sub-VFR conditions look to continue at times through at least Friday 
as shower chances persist due to coastal low pressure offshore.
Conditions look to slowly improve Friday afternoon and night as
coastal low pressure lifts north of the region. VFR conditions 
should prevail through the weekend although intermittent periods
of sub-VFR remain possible Sunday into early next week for 
terminals mainly along and east of I-95 as coastal low pressure 
remains nearby. Increased north to northeasterly flow is 
expected through Friday. Gusts of 15 to 25 kts are possible, 
especially at terminals near the waters.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories remain in effect in the main stem of the
Bay through noon within northerly flow. There will likely be a 
small lull in the winds this afternoon before they pick up 
again in earnest within northeasterly flow later tonight into 
tomorrow as high pressure strengthens to our north. A prolonged 
period of northeasterly winds is expected through Wednesday with
that area of high pressure in place. Small Craft Advisories 
have been issued again starting tonight and continuing through 
Tuesday night. At least high-end Small Craft Advisory gusts will
continue within northeasterly flow through at least Wednesday. 
Gale gusts can't be ruled out late Wednesday into Thursday 
across the waters surrounding southern Maryland.

High end Small Craft Advisory conditions will continue through 
Friday due to increased onshore north to northeasterly flow. 
Expect gusts between 20-25 kts with 30 kt gusts sporadically 
sprinkled over the middle and open waters. On and off showers 
are also possible at times as multiple shortwave disturbances 
pivot through. SCA conditions will likely continue through the 
weekend as low pressure remains off the Mid-Atalntic coast. 
Strongest gusts will be over the Chesapeake Bay and lower tidal
Potomac River.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
A cold front will pass south of the waters today. North to
northeasterly flow will lead to decreasing anomalies today, with
no coastal flooding anticipated. That will be short-lived,
however, as tides are expected to snap back to the north, with
anomalies rapidly rising again later tonight through the day
tomorrow. Elevated tide levels are then expected through much 
of the week as a strong area of high pressure builds to our 
north, leading to persistent onshore flow. The wind direction
will be closer to northeasterly rather than easterly, so the
tidal levels are expected to increase with southward extent in
the Chesapeake Bay. Many locations will likely reach Minor 
Flood Stage on Tuesday and Wednesday, and Annapolis could come 
close to flooding tonight as well. Moderate flooding can't be 
ruled out at some locations, especially Annapolis. A coastal 
low is expected to develop offshore later this week, potentially
prolonging coastal flood concerns.
